spots.old_text: - **Contract or policy benefits generally.** The old test (needed for the role, and normal business practice) is replaced by the FTA's own cases and conditions. Check them before claiming.

actual_current_destinations.text: - **Contract or policy benefits generally.** The old test (needed for the role, and normal business practice) is replaced by the six cases in [FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026](https://tax.gov.ae/Datafolder/Files/Pdf/2026/legislation/FTA%20Decision%20No.%2017%20of%202026%20on%20the%20Cases%20and%20Conditions%20for%20the%20Recovery%20of%20Input%20Tax%20Incurred%20on%20Employee%20Expenses%20-%20Publishing.pdf), issued 9 September 2026 and in force from 1 October 2026 (the FTA publishes it as an unofficial translation). A benefit outside these cases is not within exception (2):
1. **Transport:** only between home and work or client premises, or directly for the job; not for personal benefit; the employee cannot opt for cash instead.

2. **Food and drink:** the home is remote, distant or isolated; no suitable food preparation facilities at home or work and no nearby restaurants; linked to the work or required residence period; no cash option.

3. **Accommodation:** no cash option; tied to operational needs and not part of benefits or ordinary pay; the work requires living near the workplace, site or client; for the employee alone, with no family or personal use, unless the employee must live permanently near the workplace so that this is the usual home; commensurate with the job and basic needs, with no significant recreational or personal elements.
4. **New employees' accommodation:** temporary, no longer than 30 days, and commensurate with the job and basic needs.

5. **Phones, airtime, data and home internet:** necessary for the job; limited to work, or personal use is incidental and insignificant and is not the primary purpose; a documented internal policy states the permitted use and consequences of misuse; reasonable monitoring to verify compliance, retaining relevant records and justifications where use is unauthorised.

6. **Parking fees:** solely for business and tied to the job or business visits; a documented reimbursement policy specifying eligible cases and the applicable approval mechanism; receipts showing date, time, amount and tax.

spots.old_text: **Case 5: health insurance and accommodation, VAT-registered employer.** An employer buys family health cover for an employee with a spouse and four children (ages 4, 9, 14 and 19) and, from October 2026, pays for a serviced apartment for the employee. Input tax on the cover for the employee, spouse and the three children under 18 is recoverable under exception (3). The cover for the 19-year-old is outside exception (3), so its input tax is blocked unless another exception applies. A serviced apartment is not a "residential building" for VAT, so its charge carries VAT. Input tax on the October 2026 serviced-apartment charge is blocked unless a MOHRE decision or directive makes that accommodation mandatory, or the case falls within the contract-or-policy cases the FTA specifies; until those cases are published, do not claim it without checking. Had the employer instead leased an ordinary residential flat for more than six months (or to a tenant holding an Emirates ID card), the lease would be exempt: there would be no input tax on the rent, and the Article 53 change would not arise.

actual_current_destinations.text: **Case 5: health insurance and accommodation, VAT-registered employer.** An employer buys family health cover for an employee with a spouse and four children (ages 4, 9, 14 and 19) and, from October 2026, pays for a serviced apartment for the employee. Input tax on the cover for the employee, spouse and the three children under 18 is recoverable under exception (3). The cover for the 19-year-old is outside exception (3), so its input tax is blocked unless another exception applies. A serviced apartment is excluded from the residential-building definition. In this example assume its supplier makes a standard-rated taxable supply; the exclusion itself does not establish registration or every other VAT condition. Input tax on the October 2026 serviced-apartment charge is blocked unless a MOHRE decision or directive makes that accommodation mandatory, or a contract or documented policy provides it and every condition of case 3 of FTA Decision No. 17 of 2026 is met (or case 4, for a new employee, up to 30 days). If the employee could take a housing allowance instead, or the apartment is part of the ordinary package, it fails case 3. Had the employer instead leased an ordinary residential flat for more than six months (or to a tenant holding an Emirates ID card), the lease would be exempt: there would be no input tax on the rent, and the Article 53 change would not arise.
